value: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1), Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025
detail: Section 71119 of P.L. 119-21 created the Medicaid community engagement requirement (work requirement) as a condition of eligibility for specified Medicaid enrollees, adding section 1902(xx) to the Social Security Act.
notes: CRS Report R48755 identifies section 71119 as the Medicaid community engagement provision.

value: Non-pregnant adults ages 19-64 not entitled to or enrolled in Medicare
detail: Applies to individuals eligible for or enrolled in the Medicaid adult group (the ACA expansion group) or in certain section 1115 demonstrations providing minimum essential coverage. CMS reports 43 states plus DC cover these populations and must implement; U.S. territories are not subject.
notes: These are called applicable individuals.

value: 80 hours per month (about 20 hours per week)
detail: Applicable individuals must demonstrate 80 hours per month of qualifying activities, or satisfy the income alternative, or qualify for an exemption.

value: Work; community service; work program; at least half-time educational program; or any combination totaling 80 hours
detail: Individuals may combine activities to meet the 80-hour requirement.
notes: Federal definitions at 42 CFR 435.552(b): community service must be a structured public/nonprofit program that tracks hours; a work program excludes a stand-alone supervised job-search program (job search may only be a subsidiary activity under half the hours). Less-than-half-time school hours may be combined (credit hours x 3 x 4.33 weeks).

value: Monthly income of at least 80 x the federal hourly minimum wage ($580 per month in 2026)
detail: An individual can satisfy the requirement for a month with monthly income at or above 80 times the federal minimum wage instead of logging hours. Federal regulation 42 CFR 435.552(f)(2) measures that monthly income as the individual's MAGI-based income for their MAGI-based household (42 CFR 435.603) - so unearned MAGI income (net rental, interest, capital/trading gains) counts; California statute Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(e)(6) (AB 2161) uses the same MAGI-based method. DHCS member materials describe it as income from any source.
notes: Federal minimum wage $7.25 x 80 = $580. DHCS outreach letter: income from any source of at least $580 (before taxes). MAGI-based measurement re-verified 2026-10-18 against eCFR 42 CFR 435.552(f) and AB 2161 text; earlier DHCS 'total gross income' phrasing was preliminary (see FL-06).

value: Average monthly income of at least $580 over the preceding 6 months
detail: The 6-month averaging route in federal law/regulation is for a 'seasonal worker' as described in Internal Revenue Code 45R(d)(5)(B): average monthly MAGI-based income over the preceding 6 months of at least $580 (42 CFR 435.552(g)). DHCS preliminary/member wording also describes averaging for people whose hours change frequently or with fluctuating income - whether mere income fluctuation (e.g., variable trading gains) qualifies without seasonal-worker status is flagged (FL-11).
notes: DHCS H.R. 1 Implementation Plan and MEDIL I26-25 describe averaging more broadly; do not assume variable Kalshi gains can be averaged - confirm with the county.

value: Work = work for money, in-kind work, or unpaid work (other than community service); self-employment counts
detail: 42 CFR 435.552(b) defines work as work in exchange for money, work in exchange for goods or services (in-kind), and unpaid work other than community service. The CMS-2454-IFC preamble (91 FR 33348) states individuals need not be employees: people who work for themselves by starting/owning a business or as independent contractors meet the definition. DHCS ACWDL 25-30 likewise lists 'at least 80 hours of work' as including self-employment.
notes: Replaces the earlier out-of-state citation with the controlling federal definition + California ACWDL 25-30. Whether hours trading one's own account or managing one's own rentals are 'work' is still not addressed officially - see FL-02/FL-12. Trading gains are not self-employment earnings for tax purposes (IRS Topic 429), which is a separate question from the Medicaid work definition.

value: No later than January 1, 2027 (states may implement earlier)
detail: CMS states that states must generally implement the requirement no later than January 1, 2027; some states began earlier (for example Nebraska on May 1, 2026).
notes: CRS describes the effective date as December 31, 2026 or earlier at state option; see flagged items for the date-framing difference.

value: CMS-2454-IFC issued June 1, 2026; published in the Federal Register June 3, 2026 (91 FR 33348); effective July 31, 2026
detail: Interim final rule with comment period implementing section 1902(xx) of the Social Security Act; comment period closed July 31, 2026.

value: At application and at renewal; states may verify more frequently
detail: States verify compliance of applicable individuals at application, at renewal, and at state option at more frequent periodic intervals. California preliminary guidance (ACWDL 25-30) verifies only at application and six-month renewal, and states counties shall not assess the requirement merely because a member reports a change in circumstances.

value: California: applicants - the month immediately before application; enrollees - any one month between determinations
detail: Federal framing: new applicants meet the requirement for at least one month before applying; existing beneficiaries for one or more months between renewals. California law (Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(d), as amended by AB 2161) fixes the California test: an applicant must demonstrate engagement for the one month immediately preceding the application month; an enrolled person must demonstrate it for any one month between their most recent (re)determination and the next scheduled redetermination. It is therefore NOT an every-month test in California. ACWDL 25-30 gives worked examples (e.g., one qualifying month out of six at renewal suffices; months need not be consecutive).
source_name: California Legislative Information - AB 2161 (Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(d))
notes: Corrects any 'each month' phrasing elsewhere. If an applicant first becomes compliant while the application is pending, ACWDL 25-30 sets aid to begin the first day of the month after the compliance month, with earlier months denied (preliminary guidance).

value: 30-calendar-day cure period, then denial or disenrollment; reapplication allowed at any time
detail: If a state cannot verify compliance it must send a notice of noncompliance and provide 30 calendar days to demonstrate compliance or that the requirement does not apply; failing that, the application may be denied or the individual disenrolled. Disenrolled individuals may reapply at any time and are assessed on reapplication. California adds: coverage continues during the 30-day period (and at renewal, active eligibility is maintained at least through the end of that month); notice is deemed received 5 days after its date; self-attested non-receipt is good cause; denial/disenrollment occurs no later than the end of the following month, only after checking every other basis of eligibility and offering a fair hearing (AB 2161, Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(k)-(n)).
notes: No fixed lockout period appears in the CMS fact sheet. See also CA-14: California preliminary guidance allows return without a new application during a 90-day cure period after discontinuance once compliance is shown.

value: Expansion adults renew eligibility every 6 months instead of every 12
detail: Section 71107 of P.L. 119-21 requires states to conduct eligibility redeterminations for the MAGI New Adult Group every six months, effective January 1, 2027. Tribal members, pregnant or 12-month postpartum members, and children are not subject.
notes: California begins six-month checks March 1, 2027 (see California implementation table).

value: Compliance turns on hours of qualifying activity or monthly income, not on having a job or earned income
detail: $0 earned income does not by itself disqualify or satisfy the requirement; DHCS member materials allow income from any source to satisfy the $580 monthly standard.

value: $325.6 billion reduction in federal Medicaid outlays FY2025-FY2034
detail: CBO also estimated the community engagement provision would result in an average of 4.5 million more uninsured people per year FY2027-FY2034.

value: CMS released initial guidance to states in December 2025
detail: CMS issued a Center for Medicaid and CHIP Services Information Bulletin on implementing work and community engagement requirements on December 8, 2025.
source_name: CMS guidance via DHCS Tracking page

item: Losing Medi-Cal for noncompliance blocks Covered California financial help
value: No subsidized Covered California fallback if denied/disenrolled solely for work-rule noncompliance
detail: DHCS member outreach letter (MEDIL I26-25): 'If you lose Medi-Cal because you did not meet these rules, you cannot get financial help to pay for a health plan through Covered California. That means you would have to pay the full cost of new health insurance.' ACWDL 25-30 states the same for applicants and requires evaluation for all other Medi-Cal programs instead. This is distinct from having MAGI above Medi-Cal limits, where subsidized Covered California remains available with no work test.
source_name: DHCS MEDIL I26-25 member outreach letter (Sept 11, 2026)
notes: Practical consequence: do not treat subsidized marketplace coverage as a safety valve for failing the Medi-Cal work rule at MAGI at or below 138% FPL. Reapplying for Medi-Cal at any time remains allowed.

value: Agency may convert monthly MAGI-based income under $580 into work hours (income / $7.25) to combine toward 80 hours
detail: 42 CFR 435.552(e)(2): if monthly income is below 80 x federal minimum wage and the agency lacks documentation of hours worked, the agency may calculate work hours by dividing MAGI-based monthly income by the federal minimum wage, using a reasonable method to allocate hours between household members; those hours can be combined with other activities. Whether/how California will use this option has not been confirmed in published DHCS guidance reviewed.
notes: Federal option verified; California adoption unverified - ask the county before relying on a partial-income + partial-hours combination.

item: Dual official name of the law
value: P.L. 119-21 is cited both as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and as the Working Families Tax Cuts Act (WFTCA / WFTCL)
detail: CMS's own guidance states: 'Public Law (P.L.) 119-21, known as the Working Families Tax Cut Act (WFTCA), which was signed into law on July 4, 2025.' The 2027 federal payment-parameters rule cites 'Section 71305 of the WFTC legislation.' Both names refer to the same July 4, 2025 law.
notes: See flagged item FL-20: the IRS attributes the APTC repayment change to the 'Working Families Tax Cuts Act' while CRS attributes PTC provisions to P.L. 119-21 - same statute, different name.

item: How many compliant months are needed at renewal
value: Any ONE month between the last determination and the next renewal (months need not be consecutive)
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30: at the six-month renewal 'the county must determine whether the individual met the community engagement requirement in any one month since the last eligibility determination... Participation in one or more months (which do not have to be consecutive) within this period is sufficient.' DHCS worked example: income of at least $580 in one month of the renewal period satisfies the renewal.
notes: California statute WIC 14005.69(d)(2) uses the same one-month standard for enrolled members.

item: Compliance is assessed person by person
value: Each individual must independently meet the criteria; one person's compliance cannot satisfy another's
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30: 'Medi-Cal eligibility is determined at the individual level, as outlined in ACWDL 16-16... All individuals must independently meet the participation criteria; one individual's compliance cannot be used to satisfy another's requirement.' The letter's two-adult household example holds that a working partner's 100 hours cannot be used by the other applicant.
notes: Conflicts with secondary-source statements that the $580 can be 'deemed from other household members' - see flagged item FL-16.

value: The calendar month immediately preceding the month of application
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30, 'Verification and Timing of Compliance Definitions': 'For applications, the look-back month is the calendar month immediately preceding the month in which the eligibility determination is made.' Counties shall verify compliance in the month immediately prior to the month of application.
notes: California statute WIC 14005.69(d)(1) states the same: one month immediately preceding the month during which the individual applies.

item: Cure period after coverage ends for noncompliance
value: 90-day cure period to return without a new application; reapplication allowed at any time after that
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30: 'Existing Medi-Cal members who cannot meet the work and community engagement requirement may return to coverage without a new application during the 90-day cure period once they provide information demonstrating compliance with the requirement. After the 90-day cure period, they can re-apply for Medi-Cal at any time.'
notes: Distinct from the 30-calendar-day notice-of-noncompliance period, which is not additional time to satisfy the requirement after failing it initially.

value: Minimum 10 days' notice for existing members
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30: counties 'shall issue a notice of action, allowing a minimum of 10 days' notice for existing Medi-Cal members, when an individual is discontinued or denied due to noncompliance.'
notes: AB 2161 adds a written notice and fair-hearing right before denial or disenrollment.

value: The HHS Secretary is prohibited from waiving the requirement under Medicaid section 1115 demonstration authority
detail: CRS Report R48755, Table 1 (Medicaid column): 'The HHS Secretary is prohibited from waiving these requirements under the Medicaid Section 1115 demonstration waiver authority.'

value: States may request exemptions that expire no later than December 31, 2028
detail: CRS Report R48755: 'states may request exemptions if they demonstrate a "good faith effort" to comply with the community engagement requirements (as defined in statute). If approved by the HHS Secretary, such exemptions expire no later than December 31, 2028, and may be terminated by the HHS Secretary earlier if states are not meeting specified actions toward compliance.'
notes: No source located stating whether California requested such an exemption; left out rather than inferred.

value: Enrolled in an educational program at least half-time
detail: Welfare and Institutions Code section 14005.69(e)(4), as amended by AB 2161 (Chapter 209, Statutes of 2026): 'The individual is enrolled in an educational program at least half-time.'
notes: DHCS ACWDL 25-30's table says 'part-time or full-time' and the DHCS member letter says 'at least part time' - see flagged item FL-14.

item: What counts as an educational program (California statute)
value: Institution of higher education; career and technical education program; a high school; or a state-approved high-school-equivalence program of study
detail: WIC 14005.69(b)(3), as amended by AB 2161, defines 'educational program' to include an institution of higher education (20 U.S.C. 1001), a program of career and technical education (20 U.S.C. 2302), a high school (20 U.S.C. 7801), and a state-approved program of study leading to a certificate of high school equivalence.
notes: ACWDL 25-30 also lists GED/HSET preparation and adult literacy programs.

item: Notice of noncompliance - when it counts as received
value: Deemed received 5 days after the date on the notice; self-attestation of non-receipt is good cause
detail: WIC 14005.69(k)(2), as amended by AB 2161: 'an applicable individual is deemed to have received the notice of noncompliance five days after the date on the notice. Self-attestation by an applicable individual that the individual did not receive a timely notice constitutes good cause for not providing a satisfactory showing.'

value: DHCS must adopt regulations by July 1, 2029; until then it may implement by plan or county letters, information notices, or bulletins
detail: WIC 14005.69(o), as amended by AB 2161: DHCS may implement, interpret, or make specific the section 'by means of plan or county letters, information notices, plan or provider bulletins, or other similar instructions, until regulations are adopted,' and 'shall adopt regulations by July 1, 2029.'
notes: Explains why ACWDLs/MEDILs are the operative guidance and why they are labelled preliminary. Subdivision letters follow the AB 2161 chaptered text. The consolidated code display at leginfo currently ends at subdivision (n), so this letter cannot be confirmed from the display; see flagged items FL-28 and FL-29. The quoted requirement is unchanged either way.

value: Implemented only after the director certifies systems are programmed, and only to the extent federal approvals are obtained and federal financial participation is available
detail: WIC 14005.69(q), as amended by AB 2161: 'This section shall be implemented only after the director determines, and communicates in writing to the Department of Finance, that systems have been programmed for implementation of this section' and 'only to the extent that any necessary federal approvals are obtained and that federal financial participation is available and not otherwise jeopardized.'
notes: Subdivision letters follow the AB 2161 chaptered text. The consolidated code display at leginfo currently ends at subdivision (n), so this letter cannot be confirmed from the display; see flagged items FL-28 and FL-29. The quoted requirement is unchanged either way.

value: DHCS may defer implementation of a change that needs an unappropriated additional appropriation, and must publish notice of any deferral
detail: WIC 14005.69(r), as amended by AB 2161, allows deferral until the appropriation is made, with notification to the Legislature's fiscal and policy committees and publication on DHCS's website.
notes: Subdivision letters follow the AB 2161 chaptered text. The consolidated code display at leginfo currently ends at subdivision (n), so this letter cannot be confirmed from the display; see flagged items FL-28 and FL-29. The quoted requirement is unchanged either way.

value: Prior to P.L. 119-21 there was no statutory Medicaid work or community engagement requirement
detail: CRS Report R48755: 'Prior to the enactment of P.L. 119-21, there was no statutory requirement for Medicaid enrollees comparable to the new community engagement requirement, although the new statutory provision builds on the first Trump Administration's Medicaid Section 1115 demonstration waiver initiative.'
notes: California has no separate state work requirement; the state statute implements the federal one.

item: Populations excluded from the requirement in California
value: Members in any coverage group other than the MAGI New Adult Group, plus restricted-scope (emergency) Medi-Cal and pregnancy-services-only cases
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30, 'Excluded Populations': 'Members who receive Medi-Cal under other coverage groups such as Non-MAGI..., Mandatory Children's Group, or Pregnancy Group are excluded... Additionally, individuals eligible for restricted-scope (emergency) Medi-Cal or pregnancy services are also not subject to work and community engagement requirements.'

value: Immediately exempt for the pregnancy and 12 months afterward, regardless of outcome
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30: 'When an individual reports a pregnancy or the birth of a child or other termination of a pregnancy, the individual becomes immediately exempt from the work and community engagement requirement for the duration of the pregnancy and for 12 months following the end of the pregnancy, regardless of the outcome.'

value: The receiving county must accept the current status, including a verified exemption or work activity, without reassessment until the next scheduled renewal
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30: 'When a member... moves from one county to another and requests an intercounty transfer, the receiving county shall accept the member's current eligibility status, including any verified exemption or work activities, without interruption.'

value: Counties shall not assess the work requirement when a member reports a change in circumstance
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30: 'Counties shall not assess if someone is meeting the work and community engagement requirement when they report a change in circumstance to the county.' Anyone newly applying to an existing case is assessed as a new applicant if they fall in the MAGI New Adult Group.

value: 'Have a job (working at least 80 hours a month) including self-employment'
detail: DHCS ACWDL 25-30 qualifying-activities table lists 'At least 80 hours of work' with the definition 'Have a job (working at least 80 hours a month) including self-employment.' Louisiana's official Medicaid page likewise lists 'Working (including self-employment, seasonal employment, unpaid work or internship).'
notes: Re-sourced 2026-10-18 from Louisiana LDH to the California county letter. Whether hours spent personally trading on Kalshi count is still unverified (FL-02).
